description: How a screen whose ONLY showcase reference is a mobile mockup (referenceType: approved-pattern) should be read for a desktop Web implementation — the rule that stops a mobile-only reference from being mis-scored as a desktop layout defect.
rule: A mobile mockup shows CONTENT and HIERARCHY (what appears, in what order, with what emphasis) — it does not show a desktop layout, because none was assembled. A correct desktop adaptation preserves the mobile mockup's content/hierarchy while applying standard desktop layout rules (wider content column up to form-width-cap or grid.maxContentWidth, side-by-side composition where the mobile version stacked purely for narrow-viewport reasons, horizontal-row card variants where a vertical-stack mobile card would waste horizontal space).

knownCorrectAdaptations.desktopForm: horizontal-row courseProgressCard (.mtx-progress-row) — a deliberate, correct desktop-appropriate adaptation, not a defect (design-to-code/screens/my-learning.json).

knownCorrectAdaptations.mobileForm: stacked hero (thumbnail above meta), sticky bottom CTA
knownCorrectAdaptations.desktopForm: hero stacks side-by-side where width allows; CTA inline, not sticky (page short enough at Desktop widths).

misreadingToAvoid: Never score a desktop implementation against a mobile mockup as if the mobile mockup were itself the desktop target — that conflates 'different from the reference image' with 'wrong,' when the reference image was never a desktop composition in the first place.
